identity.title: P53-assisted METTL14-mediated m(6)A modification of SLC7A11 drives ferroptosis and inflammation in polycystic ovary syndrome.

content.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by chronic inflammation and follicular arrest, yet the molecular drivers linking these pathologies to granulosa cell (GC) death remain elusive. Here, we identify a ferroptosis-inflammation cascade as a critical determinant of ovarian dysfunction in PCOS. We demonstrate that the N(6)-methyladenosine (m(6)A) methyltransferase METTL14 is aberrantly upregulated in human PCOS GCs, correlating with oxidative damage. Mechanistically, we uncover a non-canonical paradigm where upregulated P53 functions as an essential RNA-binding cofactor, recruiting METTL14 to the SLC7A11 transcript. Validated by AlphaFold3 modeling, this METTL14-p53 complex catalyzes SLC7A11 m(6)A hypermethylation and mRNA destabilization. The resulting SLC7A11 deficiency dismantles antioxidant defenses, driving ferroptosis and amplifying local inflammation. Crucially, in a DHEA-induced PCOS rat model, genetic ablation of Tp53 severed this pathogenic axis, restoring redox balance, suppressing inflammation, and reversing the polycystic phenotype. Collectively, our findings reveal a pivotal epigenetic mechanism linking m(6)A reprogramming, iron-dependent cell death, and inflammation, highlighting the METTL14-p53-SLC7A11 axis as a therapeutic target in PCOS.
